title: Insomnia
text: Difficulty falling asleep, maintaining sleep, or early morning awakening with inability to return to sleep, causing significant distress.

title: Hypersomnia
text: Excessive sleepiness despite a main sleep period lasting at least 7 hours, or difficulty being fully awake after abrupt awakening.

title: Nightmares
text: Extended, extremely dysphoric, and well-remembered dreams that usually involve efforts to avoid threats to survival, security, or physical integrity.

title: Sleep terrors
text: Recurrent episodes of abrupt terror arousal from sleep, usually beginning with a panicky scream, accompanied by autonomic arousal (heart racing, sweating).

title: Panic attack
text: An abrupt surge of intense fear or intense discomfort that reaches a peak within minutes, accompanied by physical symptoms like palpitations, sweating, trembling, shortness of breath, or fear of dying.

title: Flashbacks
text: Dissociative reactions in which the individual feels or acts as if the traumatic event were recurring. (Such reactions may occur on a continuum, with the most extreme expression being a complete loss of awareness of present surroundings).

title: Hypervigilance
text: A state of increased alertness and sensitivity to surroundings, often accompanied by behavior aimed at preventing danger (e.g., constantly scanning the environment).

title: Exaggerated startle response
text: An involuntary, strong, and rapid reaction to a sudden or unexpected stimulus (noise, movement), often seen in PTSD.

title: Excessive or inappropriate guilt
text: Feelings of guilt which may be delusional or merely excessive regarding minor past failings, often seen in major depressive episodes.

title: Feelings of worthlessness
text: Persistent sense of having no value or worth, self-hatred, or belief that one is a burden to others.

title: Emotional numbing
text: Inability to experience the full range of emotions, feeling detached from others, or feeling 'empty'.

title: Irritability or anger outbursts
text: Persistent anger or irritability, often disproportionate to the situation, resulting in verbal or physical aggression toward people or objects.

title: Mood lability (Mood swings)
text: Rapid and extreme shifts in mood, for example, from laughter to tears or from calm to anger, within a short period.
